claims.claim: Check Point positioned its 2026 product strategy around an AI Network Firewall and AI Defense plane intended to secure enterprise adoption of AI across users, applications and agents, indicating expansion of its addressable security surface with enterprise AI adoption.

risks.risk: AI-security positioning is strategically relevant but the release does not isolate revenue contribution or win rates for the new AI products.

unknowns.unknown: Adoption, pricing and competitive displacement attributable to AI Network Firewall and AI Defense are not quantified in the retrieved primary source.

claims.claim: Check Point reported Q2 2026 revenue of $674 million, up 1% year over year; security subscription revenue of $333 million, up 12%; RPO of $2.6 billion, up 7%; and non-GAAP operating margin of 39%.
Management said Q2 results were in line with expectations while sales capacity was being expanded; the company also repurchased about $325 million of shares during Q2 under an expanded authorization.

risks.risk: Total revenue growth remains modest despite stronger subscription growth, so execution must prove that expanded sales capacity converts into durable acceleration.

contradictions.contradiction: Security subscription revenue grew 12% while total revenue grew only 1%, showing mix strength without broad top-line acceleration.

unknowns.unknown: Return on incremental sales-capacity investment and contribution from newer AI-security products remain unquantified.
